readRepoEntry rejects each malformed level and accepts missing parts
mergeRepoEntryKeys changes only the named keys
concurrent writes all land one at a time and a failure does not stall the queue
write-failed leaves the file and temp file as they were
verify step re-merges after an outside change and returns file-changed after the bounded attempts

get returns what set wrote and shows an outside write

ensure writes the five keys once and concurrent sets both land

titles.title: buildRepoSettings values, resolved target and policy rows
sign-in mapping for every whoAmI outcome
repo identity uses the exact registered path
get returns what set wrote and shows an outside write
set refuses read-only, unknown, invalid and unregistered inputs and writes nothing
only the signed-in-user read runs through s1's adapter
malformed files return repo-config-unreadable and keep their bytes
get reads once, never writes, and resolves from the git remote when there is no own target
ensure writes the five keys once and concurrent sets both land
the gitHooks setting reads false when absent, is validated as a boolean and round-trips through repo-config.json

applyBuildDefaults writes the type's typecheck and test commands and resultFormat exit-code together for a Python, Go, Rust and JVM repo with no build key, and writes nothing for a Node repo, an unknown repo and an entry that already sets any of the three keys
applyBuildDefaults never throws and reports write-failed when the entry cannot be read or the write fails, leaving no lone command
repo.settings.get returns buildSetup with the type, the commands source and the suggestion for a repo with none, and writes nothing

migrateBuildDefaults writes the typecheck and test commands and resultFormat exit-code together for each Python, Go, Rust and JVM repo with none of them, and writes nothing for a Node repo, an unknown repo, a repo whose directory is gone and an entry that sets any one of the three keys
migrateBuildDefaults run twice changes nothing the second time and reports already-set for the repos the first run set, and a user's own value set between the runs is kept

migrateBuildDefaults keeps going when one repo's write is refused or throws, reports write-failed with its note for that repo only, and reports write-failed for every repo, leaving the file as it was, when repo-config.json is malformed

the repo.buildDefaults.migrate handler returns ok, one entry per registered repo in registry order and counts with a key for every outcome that add up to the number of repos, returns zero counts for no repos, and returns registry-unreadable as data when the registry cannot be listed, writing nothing
